fieldNotes.location: Roster coords (44.316671,-123.107215 / 31831 Cartney Dr) landed in farmland ~8 km SE of the mill. The GP Halsey / Cascade Pacific Pulp mill is at 30470-30480 American Drive, NW of Halsey town. Located via EPA FRS bounding box; mill core locked at 44.3792,-123.1605.
fieldNotes.truckGate: Single dedicated access road off American Drive is the only land route into the operational yard. Integrated pulp+tissue mill (~250-550 employees) is a controlled-access site. The security checkpoint is internal on the access road; Street View covers only public roads and did not reach it.
fieldNotes.guardShack: Inferred from facility scale and shared dual-operator campus (Cascade Pacific Pulp kraft mill + GP tissue mill); a manned booth is standard. Booth not positively resolved overhead — flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: Co-located dual operation: Cascade Pacific Pulp kraft market-pulp mill (30480 American Dr) and Georgia-Pacific tissue/towel mill (30470 American Dr) share the campus, plus large recovery boiler / power buildings and converting plant.
fieldNotes.railServed: Rail line runs along the west side through the property; tank cars observed parked on the spur in Street View (May 2024).
fieldNotes.dropArea: Large multi-row drop yard south of the converting building — clear rows totaling ~50+ parked trailers (green, white, orange dry-vans), with room for ~90.
fieldNotes.scale: Inbound wood-chip / log truck traffic at a mill of this scale uses a truck scale; consistent with the access-road layout but not definitively resolved overhead.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Inbound wood chips to the chip yard (NE); finished tissue/pulp ships from warehouse/converting docks (S/SW) — physically separate.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: ~20 estimated across the converting/warehouse south face; partly obscured by trailers and process equipment; low confidence.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Wide paved aprons at the drop yard and access road provide ample unused width for a bypass lane.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Mill sits in open Willamette Valley farmland NW of the small town of Halsey. Rural.
